body:
## Problem

Finding class: misconfiguration (missing trust-boundary check). `serveNFS` listens on 127.0.0.1 and serves go-nfs's `NullAuthHandler`, which accepts AUTH_NULL, with no check on who connects. Any process of any local account can mount `127.0.0.1:<port>` and read, write and delete the whole share with the mounting user's WebDAV credentials. The README presents the loopback listener as the design and never mentions this.

## Evidence

Detected by manual review (no scanner models this).

- `internal/server/server.go:169`: `ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, no filter wraps the listener.
- `internal/server/server.go:174`: `helpers.NewNullAuthHandler(bfs)`; its `Mount` returns `[]nfs.AuthFlavor{nfs.AuthFlavorNull}`.
- The port is visible to every user (`lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN`, `ss -ltn`).
- Failing scenario: user B runs `mount_nfs -o vers=4,port=<port> 127.0.0.1:/ ~/x` (macOS allows non-root mounts on an owned directory) or `sudo mount -t nfs ...` on Linux and gets full access to user A's kDrive.
- A reserved-port rule alone does not close it on macOS: a non-root process could not bind `127.0.0.1:999` but could bind `0.0.0.0:999` and connect to a loopback server from source port 999 (tested on this host, macOS 27.2.1).

## Impact

On a shared Linux host, a Mac with several accounts, or any host running services as other users, those accounts get unauthenticated read/write access to the user's entire cloud drive. Deletions go to the kDrive trash; overwrites create versions that count against the quota.

## Fix

1. Wrap the NFS listener and close any connection whose source port is >= 1024. Kernel NFS clients use reserved ports by default (Linux `resvport`, macOS `resvport`), and unprivileged Linux users cannot bind below 1024 (`net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start`=1024), so this closes the hole on Linux. Log rejected peers at ERROR.
2. macOS: the port rule is bypassable (see Evidence). Additionally accept only RPCs whose AUTH_SYS uid is the daemon's uid or 0; this needs the vendored go-nfs to pass the RPC credential to the handler (record the change in `third_party/go-nfs/UPSTREAM.md`).
3. State the residual risk (a custom RPC client forging AUTH_SYS on macOS) in README Limitations.
4. Test: a connection from an ephemeral source port is closed before any RPC is answered.

## Resolution
Added go-nfs Server.Authorize (rpc-auth.patch) and ownerOnly: only the owner's AUTH_SYS uid or root is served; Linux also closes connections from unreserved ports (reservedPortListener). Patch also fixes denied replies (reject_stat value, big-endian auth_stat). Verified with a raw RPC probe: macOS uid 502 denied (reject_stat=1 auth_stat=5), owner accepted; Linux non-root connection closed, foreign uid on reserved port denied, a second account's root mount cannot list files. README documents the macOS residual risk. Unit tests in internal/server/auth_test.go.
title: Loopback NFS export accepts every local user without authentication

body:
## Problem

Finding class: dependency-vulnerability. The linked golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0 contains the deprecated `openpgp` package flagged by GO-2026-5932 ("unmaintained, unsafe by design").

## Evidence

Detected by grype (GO-2026-5932, severity Unknown), trivy (GO-2026-5932, UNKNOWN) and govulncheck. `go.mod:59`: `golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0 // indirect`. `go version -m` lists it in the built binary. govulncheck: "your code doesn't appear to call these vulnerabilities"; the `openpgp` package is not imported.

## Impact

No reachable path today. A future import of `x/crypto/openpgp` (directly or by a dependency) would inherit the flaws, and every scan reports the advisory until the version moves.

## Fix

When golang.org/x/crypto tags a release containing the fix, run `go get golang.org/x/crypto@<that tag> && go mod tidy`. The fix currently exists only as pseudo-version `v0.58.1-0.20261009181718-2f1f834330b2`; pinning that is possible but trades a tagged release for an untagged one with no reachable benefit.

## Resolution
go get golang.org/x/crypto@v0.59.0; govulncheck now reports no vulnerabilities and grype no longer matches it.
title: golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0 carries GO-2026-5932 (openpgp)

body:
## Problem

Finding class: dependency-vulnerability. go.sum lists go.opentelemetry.io/otel v1.45.0, affected by GO-2026-6975 (memory allocation amplification in W3C baggage parsing); fixed in v1.47.0.

## Evidence

Detected by grype (GO-2026-6975, Medium). `go.sum:397`. The module is not required by go.mod and not linked: `go version -m` on the built binary lists no otel module; `go mod why -m` reaches it only through `github.com/rclone/rclone/vfs.test` -> `backend/all` -> googlecloudstorage, i.e. rclone's own tests.

## Impact

None at runtime: the code is not in the binary. Scanners keep reporting it.

## Fix

No code change. Record the reachability analysis in a scanner ignore with a reason (e.g. `.grype.yaml` `ignore: - vulnerability: GO-2026-6975`) or let it drop out when rclone bumps the dependency.

## Resolution
Recorded the reachability analysis as a grype ignore with reason in .grype.yaml; grype reports 0 matches and lists it under ignoredMatches.
title: go.opentelemetry.io/otel v1.45.0 in go.sum carries GO-2026-6975

body:
## Problem

`Stop` calls the unmount callback and then shuts NFS down unconditionally. `unmountIfMounted` only logs when both unmount attempts fail, and treats an `IsMounted` error as "not mounted", so nothing tells `Stop` the mount is still there.

## Evidence

- `internal/server/server.go:198-204`: `unmount()` then `s.nfs.Shutdown(ctx)` with no check of the result.
- `main.go:98`: `if mounted, _ := platform.IsMounted(mp); !mounted { return }` discards the error.
- `main.go:106-108`: a failed forced unmount is only logged.
- The daemon passes `interactive=false` (`cmd_mount.go`, `srv.Stop(func() { unmountIfMounted(m, false) })`), so on Linux the unmount is `sudo -n umount`, which fails with "a password is required" unless sudo is NOPASSWD.
- Failing scenario (Linux): the daemon gets SIGTERM from a session logout (systemd `KillUserProcesses`) or a plain `kill`; `sudo -n umount` fails; NFS stops. The mount carries `hard` (seen in `/proc/self/mounts` during the Linux smoke run), so every later access to the mountpoint blocks in D state until root runs `umount -f -l`.

## Impact

A routine stop path leaves an unkillable hang on the user's home directory tree (file managers, shells, `ls ~`) until reboot or root intervention. The CLI `unmount` path is unaffected because it unmounts interactively before signalling.

## Fix

Have `unmountIfMounted` return whether the mountpoint is still mounted: re-check `IsMounted` after the attempts and treat an `IsMounted` error as still mounted. In `Stop` (or in the daemon command before calling it), when still mounted: log at ERROR with the exact recovery command (`nfs-mount unmount --force <name>`), keep serving, and return to `waitForSignal`; the restored default handling still lets a second signal kill the process. Document the behaviour in README Limitations. Test with a fake unmount that fails: NFS must keep serving.

## Resolution
Server.Stop no longer unmounts; serveUntilStopped unmounts first and keeps serving (re-arming signals) when the mountpoint is still mounted or the mount table cannot be read; unmountIfMounted re-checks and reports. Verified in the Linux container: user lim (sudo -n umount fails) got 'still mounted, so the server keeps running', mount stayed usable; after root umount + SIGTERM the daemon exited.
title: Daemon stops serving NFS even when its own unmount failed, stranding a hard mount

body:
## Problem

`state()` returns any `Query` error other than `ErrNotRunning` (for example a 5 s timeout from a wedged daemon) as a hard error. `unmount` returns that error before touching the mount, so `--force`, the documented escape hatch, cannot run. `status` aborts the whole listing on the first such mount, and `stopServer` retries a failing query forever with no output.

## Evidence

- `main.go:86-90`: `st, err := server.Query(...)`; only `ErrNotRunning` is absorbed, every other error is returned.
- `cmd_unmount.go:43-46`: `st, mounted, err := state(ctx, m); if err != nil { return err }` comes before the `force` branch.
- `cmd_unmount.go:93-95`: `if err != nil { continue }` loops silently.
- `internal/server/control.go`: `Query` uses `Timeout: 5 * time.Second`, so a daemon that accepts but never answers yields a timeout error, not `ErrNotRunning`.
- Failing scenario: the daemon hangs (deadlock, or blocked in a VFS walk during heavy I/O); `nfs-mount unmount --force kdrive` prints a timeout error and leaves the mount in place.

## Impact

Exactly when the server is unhealthy, the tool refuses to clear the mount, and the user must find `diskutil unmount force` or `sudo umount -f -l` themselves. `status` hides every other mount behind one bad one.

## Fix

Return the query error separately from `state()` (e.g. `(st *Status, mounted bool, queryErr error)`). In `unmount`, attempt the platform unmount whenever `mounted` is true regardless of `queryErr`, then report that the server did not answer (and its PID if known). In `status`, print `<name>: server not answering: <err>` for that mount and continue. In `stopServer`, print the error and stop waiting after a bounded number of consecutive failures.

## Resolution
state() returns queryErr separately; unmount always unmounts when mounted, status prints 'server does not answer' per mount, stopServer gives up after 10 consecutive failures. Verified on macOS with the daemon SIGSTOPped: status reported it, mount refused, unmount --force cleared the mount in 5 s.
title: unmount --force and status give up whenever the daemon does not answer

body:
## Problem

When `nfs.Server.Serve` returns an error other than `ErrServerClosed`, the goroutine logs it and exits; the daemon and its control socket keep running, so `status` still reports the share as mounted while every NFS request hangs. The control server's `Serve` error is discarded the same way.

## Evidence

- `internal/server/server.go:185-187`: `fs.Errorf(nil, "NFS server stopped: %v", err)` and nothing else.
- go-nfs `Server.Serve` (vendored `server.go`, Accept loop) returns on any non-timeout Accept error, e.g. EMFILE when the process runs out of file descriptors.
- `internal/server/control.go:65`: `go func() { _ = s.control.Serve(ln) }()`.

## Impact

A transient fd exhaustion permanently kills NFS service while everything that monitors the daemon (status, the mount table) looks healthy; processes on the mount hang until the user notices.

## Fix

Give `Server` a `Done() <-chan error` that both Serve goroutines send to on unexpected exit, and have the daemon's wait select on it alongside SIGINT/SIGTERM, then run the normal stop path (which, with the separate Stop fix, keeps the mount safe).

## Resolution
Server.Done() delivers unexpected NFS/control Serve exits; waitForStop selects on it and serveUntilStopped unmounts and stops. Not exercised end to end (no way to make the loopback listener fail on demand); covered by build, vet and review.
title: A failed NFS server leaves the daemon running and reporting healthy

body:
## Problem

`listenControl` is check-then-act: it dials the socket, removes the file, then listens. Two daemons starting together can both see no listener; the second removes the first one's socket file and listens on a new one. The first keeps serving NFS but can no longer be reached, stopped or queried by the CLI.

## Evidence

- `internal/server/control.go:40-47`: `net.Dial` probe, then `os.Remove(path)`, then `net.Listen("unix", path)`, with no lock in between.
- `cmd_mount.go` `mountBackground` checks `state()` before spawning, so two `nfs-mount mount` invocations started together (shell startup scripts, a login item plus a manual run) both spawn daemons, and both then call `platform.Mount` on the same mountpoint.

## Impact

An orphaned daemon holding the VFS cache for the same share, a second mount stacked on the mountpoint, and possibly two writers uploading from two caches.

## Fix

Take an exclusive `syscall.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on `<StateDir>/<name>.lock` before `listenControl`, keep the file open for the daemon's lifetime, and fail with "a server is already running" when the lock is held. The kernel drops the lock if the daemon dies, so stale-socket cleanup keeps working.

## Resolution
lockMount takes an exclusive flock on <name>.lock for the server's lifetime before claiming the socket. Verified: two concurrent 'nfs-mount mount' runs left one daemon and one mount, the second failing with 'a server is already running for this share'; TestLockMountExcludesSecondServer.
title: Two concurrent mount runs can start two daemons for one share

body:
## Problem

`validate` turns a relative `mountpoint` into an absolute path with `filepath.Abs`, i.e. relative to wherever the command happens to run. The control socket is keyed by name, so a later command run from another directory finds the same daemon but checks, and may mount, a different directory.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:121`: `if m.Mountpoint, err = filepath.Abs(mp); err != nil {`.
- Failing scenario: `mountpoint = "kDrive"`; `cd ~ && nfs-mount mount` mounts `~/kDrive`; later `cd /tmp && nfs-mount mount` sees the running server, finds `/tmp/kDrive` unmounted, and `attach` mounts the same server again at `/tmp/kDrive`. `status` from `/tmp` reports "server running, but /tmp/kDrive is not mounted".

## Impact

Duplicate mounts of one server and wrong status output, depending on the current directory.

## Fix

Reject relative mountpoints in `validate`: after `expandHome`, if `!filepath.IsAbs(mp)` return `errors.New("mountpoint must be absolute or start with ~/")`. Add a config test for it.

## Resolution
validate rejects mountpoints that are not absolute or ~/-prefixed; README states it; covered in TestLoadValidation.
title: A relative mountpoint resolves against each command's working directory

body:
## Problem

`xdgDir` discards the error from `os.UserHomeDir()`. With `$HOME` unset and no absolute `XDG_*` variable, the config, state and cache directories become relative paths such as `.local/state/nfs-mount`, resolved against the current directory.

## Evidence

- `internal/config/config.go:76-77`: `home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()` then `return filepath.Join(home, fallback)`.
- Failing scenario: `env -i /path/to/nfs-mount mount`, or a cron/launchd job without HOME: the daemon's socket, log and VFS cache land under the job's working directory, and `nfs-mount status` from a normal shell reports "not mounted" for a share that is mounted.

## Impact

State and cache end up in an arbitrary directory, and the tool loses track of its own daemon.

## Fix

Fail loudly instead: resolve the home directory once at startup (in `newRootCmd`'s `PersistentPreRunE`), exit with `cannot determine home directory: <err>` when it fails and no absolute XDG variable covers the path, and have `xdgDir` use the resolved value.

## Resolution
config.CheckDirs (run as the root command's PersistentPreRunE) fails when the state or cache dir would be relative; xdgDir handles the error explicitly; TestCheckDirs.
title: xdgDir ignores the UserHomeDir error and returns a relative path

body:
## Problem

The tool builds the remote and VFS options only from its own config, but rclone also reads its environment variables: `fs.ConfigMap` adds an `optionEnvVars` getter, so every WebDAV option the mount does not set is taken from `RCLONE_WEBDAV_<OPTION>`, and `vfscommon.Opt` and the global config are loaded from `RCLONE_VFS_*` and other `RCLONE_*` variables at package init. None of this is documented.

## Evidence

- `internal/server/server.go:152`: `ri.NewFs(ctx, m.Name, "", fs.ConfigMap(ri.Prefix, ri.Options, "", conf))`.
- rclone `fs/configmap.go:36-47`: `optionEnvVars.Get` looks up `OptionToEnv(prefix + "-" + key)`.
- rclone `fs/registry.go:570-577`: global option blocks are loaded via `ConfigMap("", oi.Options, "", nil)`, i.e. from the environment.
- `internal/server/server.go:115-132`: `vfsOptions` starts from `vfscommon.Opt` and overrides only the cache mode, max age and max size.
- Failing scenario: a shell with `RCLONE_VFS_READ_ONLY=true` (left over from other rclone use) gives a read-only mount with no message; `RCLONE_WEBDAV_HEADERS` adds headers to every kDrive request.

## Impact

The same config behaves differently depending on the user's shell environment, with no hint of why.

## Fix

Document it in the README Configure section: rclone's `RCLONE_*` environment variables (`RCLONE_VFS_*`, `RCLONE_WEBDAV_*`, global flags) apply to the server, and the config file wins only for `url`, `user`, the password, the vendor and the values set in `[mounts.<name>.vfs]`.

## Resolution
README Configure section documents which RCLONE_* variables apply and what the config file overrides.
title: RCLONE_* environment variables silently change the remote and the VFS

body:
## Problem

`validate` accepts both `https` and `http` URLs for any host. With `user` set, rclone's WebDAV backend sends HTTP Basic credentials on every request, so an `http://` URL to a remote host transmits the password in cleartext, and the tool says nothing.

## Evidence

`internal/config/config.go:111`: `if err != nil || (u.Scheme != "https" && u.Scheme != "http") || u.Host == "" {`.

## Impact

A typo (`http://` for `https://`) or a misconfigured server exposes the account password, often an Infomaniak application password, to anyone on the network path.

## Fix

Accept `http` only when the host is loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, checked with `net.ParseIP(...).IsLoopback()`), and reject other `http` URLs with `use https:// for <host>; http sends the password in cleartext`. Loopback keeps local test servers working.

## Resolution
validate accepts http only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1; README states it; covered in TestLoadValidation.
title: An http:// URL sends the WebDAV password in cleartext without warning

body:
## Problem

go-nfs's default logger writes through the standard `log` package, and `rlog.InitLogging` routes `log.Printf` to slog at NOTICE. Every go-nfs message, errors and debug traces alike, therefore lands in the log as NOTICE with the real level only as a text prefix.

## Evidence

- `main.go:129`: `rlog.InitLogging()`; `main.go:139`: `nfs.Log.SetLevel(nfsLevel)`, with no `nfs.SetLogger`.
- rclone `fs/log/log.go` `InitLogging`: `slog.SetLogLoggerLevel(fs.SlogLevelNotice)` ("Make log.Printf logs at level Notice").
- Observed daemon output this session: `NOTICE: [ERROR] DEBUG setattr unsupported attr 25 ...` and `NOTICE: [DEBUG] nfs4 op 15 returned status 2`.

## Impact

A grep or filter for ERROR misses go-nfs errors (the Linux smoke test's "daemon log errors: none" check would have), and `-vv` floods the NOTICE level with protocol traces.

## Fix

Add an `nfs.Logger` adapter whose `Errorf`/`Error` call `fs.Errorf`, `Warnf`/`Warn` call `fs.Logf`, `Infof`/`Info` call `fs.Infof`, and `Debugf`/`Tracef` call `fs.Debugf`, and install it with `nfs.SetLogger` in `setupLogging`, as rclone's `cmd/serve/nfs/handler.go` does.

## Resolution
nfslog.go adds an nfs.Logger adapter mapping go-nfs levels onto rclone's (installed in setupLogging). Verified: no go-nfs lines at NOTICE/mislabelled in the macOS smoke log; Linux log shows 'ERROR : Refused NFS connection'.
title: go-nfs messages are logged at NOTICE whatever their level

body:
## Problem

`ReadDir` appends every in-memory sidecar in the directory unconditionally. When a file is deleted or renamed outside this mount (web app, another device), its `._<name>` stays in memory and in the listing until the daemon restarts. Orphans also count against the 64 MiB sidecar cap, past which every extended-attribute write fails with ENOSPC.

## Evidence

- `internal/fsys/fs.go:170-172`: `if side := f.side.list(clean(dir)); len(side) > 0 { out = append(out, side...) ...`.
- `internal/fsys/sidecar.go:96-104`: `list` returns every stored sidecar whose parent matches, with no check that `<name>` still exists.
- `internal/fsys/sidecar.go:20`: `const sidecarLimit = 64 << 20`.
- Failing scenario: Obsidian saves `Tasks.md` with xattrs (creating `._Tasks.md` in memory); the note is deleted from the phone; after `dir_cache_time`, `ls -a` on the mount still shows `._Tasks.md` with no `Tasks.md`.

## Impact

Stale entries in listings, and a slow leak that ends with xattr writes failing on a long-running mount.

## Fix

In `ReadDir`, after building the remote listing, drop (and remove from the store) every in-memory `._<name>` whose `<name>` is absent from that listing. Leave `.DS_Store` alone; it belongs to the directory, not to a file. Add a test: create `x` and `._x`, delete `x` on the backing directory, list, and expect neither.

## Resolution
sidecars.list drops in-memory ._<name> entries whose <name> is missing from the remote listing (and frees their bytes); TestOrphanedAppleDoubleIsDropped.
title: In-memory AppleDouble files outlive the files they belong to

body:
## Problem

Only `internal/fsys` has tests. The packages that decide whether a share counts as mounted, how the config is read, which VFS options apply, and how the CLI talks to its daemon have none, although several hold pure logic that is cheap to test.

## Evidence

`go test ./...` reports `[no test files]` for `github.com/ivuorinen/nfs-mount`, `internal/config`, `internal/platform` and `internal/server`. Untested logic with a concrete failure mode:
- `internal/platform/mount_linux.go` `unescapeMount`: decodes `\040` in `/proc/self/mounts`; a bug makes a mountpoint with a space read as unmounted, so `mount` mounts it again.
- `internal/config/config.go` `Load` and `Mount`: unknown-key rejection, name validation, single-mount selection.
- `internal/server/server.go` `vfsOptions`: unknown-key rejection and override precedence over the built-in defaults.
- `internal/server/control.go` `Query`: the `ErrNotRunning` mapping that every command branches on.
- `cmd_mount.go` `spawnDaemon`: the ready-pipe protocol (`ok <port>` / `error: ...` / EOF).

## Impact

Regressions in mount detection, config handling or daemon start-up surface only at run time on a user's machine; the manual smoke runs that covered them are not repeatable.

## Fix

Add table tests: `unescapeMount` (plain path, `\040`, `\134`, trailing backslash); `config.Load` against temp files (unknown key, bad name, relative mountpoint once rejected, one vs several mounts); `vfsOptions` (unknown key errors, `vfs_write_back` override applied, defaults kept); `Query` against a path with no socket and against a closed listener, both `ErrNotRunning`; and the reply parsing in `spawnDaemon`, extracted into a function that takes the bytes read.

## Resolution
Added tests: config (validation, ~ expansion, mount selection, CheckDirs), platform (unescapeMount, moved to the shared unix file), server (vfsOptions, Query not-running shapes, lockMount, ownerOnly, reserved ports), main (parseReady, extracted from spawnDaemon). go test -race ./... passes.
title: Config, platform, server and CLI code have no tests

body:
## Problem

The package comment states the adapter follows rclone's and "adds one thing", the in-memory sidecar files. It also serialises open handles per file (`pathlock.go`), which changes concurrency behaviour and exists to stop lost writes.

## Evidence

`internal/fsys/fs.go:3-5`: `It follows rclone's own adapter (cmd/serve/nfs/filesystem.go) and adds one thing: sidecar files (see IsSidecar) are kept in memory instead of being uploaded.` `internal/fsys/fs.go` `OpenFile` wraps every handle in `lockedFile` from `pathlock.go`.

## Impact

A reader comparing this adapter with rclone's is told the only difference is sidecars, and could drop the path lock as an unexplained divergence, bringing back the lost-write bug.

## Fix

Reword to name both additions: "...and adds two things: sidecar files (see IsSidecar) are kept in memory instead of being uploaded, and open handles are serialised per file (see pathLocks), because overlapping open-write-close cycles lose writes in rclone's VFS cache."

## Resolution
Package doc now names both additions: in-memory sidecars and per-file handle serialisation.
title: fsys package doc says the adapter adds one thing; it adds two

body:
## Problem

README Limitations says every file is 0644 and every directory 0755. The VFS starts from 0666/0777 and masks them with the process umask, so the modes depend on the user's umask.

## Evidence

- `README.md:130`: `every file belongs to the mounting user and is 0644, directories 0755.`
- rclone `vfs/vfscommon/options.go:154-155`: `Name: "umask", Default: FileMode(getUmask())`; `Options.Init` applies `opt.FilePerms &= ^opt.Umask` and `opt.DirPerms &= ^opt.Umask`; `internal/server/server.go` `vfsOptions` calls `opt.Init(ctx)`.
- With umask 077 the mount shows 0600 and 0700.

## Impact

Users with a non-default umask see modes the documentation says cannot occur.

## Fix

Change the bullet to: "Modes and owners are not stored: every file belongs to the mounting user, with modes from your umask (0644 for files and 0755 for directories under the usual 022). Set `umask` in `[mounts.<name>.vfs]` to override."

## Resolution
README Limitations now says modes come from the umask (0644/0755 under 022) and how to override with umask in [mounts.<name>.vfs].
title: README states fixed 0644/0755 modes; modes follow the umask

body:
## Problem

There is no `LICENSE`/`COPYING` file and no SPDX header. Source without a licence is "all rights reserved": nobody else may use, modify or redistribute it. The module path `github.com/ivuorinen/nfs-mount` signals intended publication.

## Evidence

Repository root holds `.editorconfig`, `.markdownlint.json`, `README.md`, Go sources, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `internal/`, `third_party/`; no licence file. The only `LICENSE` is `third_party/go-nfs/LICENSE` (Apache-2.0, upstream's). Linked dependency licences, from the modules in the built binary: MIT 18, BSD 18, Apache-2.0 12, ISC 1 (go-xdr), CC0 1 (blake3), MPL-2.0 1 (golang-lru, unmodified); no GPL/LGPL/AGPL. CodeQL was not run because of this (its terms need an OSI licence).

## Impact

Becomes High the moment the repository is public: others cannot legally use it, and contributions arrive without a licence grant.

## Fix

The owner chooses a licence; every linked dependency is compatible with MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0 or GPL. Add it as `LICENSE` at the repository root and mention it in the README. If binaries are ever distributed, also ship the dependency notices (Apache-2.0 for go-nfs, MIT/BSD texts).

## Resolution
Added MIT LICENSE (owner's choice) and a License section in the README naming the Apache-2.0 vendored go-nfs.
title: The project declares no licence

body:
## Problem

No `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, while the repo has enforced conventions a contributor cannot discover from the README: the build, the test runner and its slow test, two-platform linting, markdown and editorconfig checks, and the procedure for updating the vendored go-nfs.

## Evidence

All three paths absent. Enforced conventions present: `go.mod` (Go 1.27.4 build), `go test` (with `TestConcurrentWrites` skipped under `-short`), `golangci-lint` (run for darwin and linux), `.markdownlint.json`, `.editorconfig`, `third_party/go-nfs/UPSTREAM.md` (patch-update procedure).

## Impact

A contributor does not learn that lint must pass for both GOOS values, that the slow concurrency test exists, or how the go-nfs patch is maintained, and changes land that break the Linux build or the vendored patch.

## Fix

Scaffold `CONTRIBUTING.md` from the real conventions, offered through the apply-fixes prompt: setup (Go 1.27), build (`go build -o ~/.local/bin/nfs-mount .`), tests (`go test ./...`, `go test -short ./...` for the quick loop), lint (`golangci-lint run ./...` and `GOOS=linux golangci-lint run ./...`, `markdownlint-cli2 README.md`, `editorconfig-checker`), the vendored go-nfs update procedure (link `third_party/go-nfs/UPSTREAM.md`), and how to smoke-test a mount against a local WebDAV server.

## Resolution
Scaffolded CONTRIBUTING.md from real tooling: requirements, layout, build/test/lint for both GOOS, vendored go-nfs procedure, local and Linux smoke tests (the rclone --config /dev/null serve webdav step was used in this run's macOS smoke test).
title: CONTRIBUTING.md is absent in a repo with a build system and test runner

body:
## Problem

The repository has no `.gitignore`. `go build` without `-o` writes a ~26 MB `nfs-mount` binary into the repository root, where `git status` lists it as untracked and a careless add commits it.

## Evidence

`ls -A` at the root shows no `.gitignore`; `git status --short` (after `git init`) lists every file as untracked with nothing ignored. The README's build command uses `-o ~/.local/bin/nfs-mount`, but `go build .` is the default habit.

## Impact

A committed binary bloats history permanently (removal needs a history rewrite).

## Fix

Add `.gitignore` containing `/nfs-mount` (the default `go build` output name).

## Resolution
Added .gitignore with /nfs-mount.
title: No .gitignore: a plain go build drops the binary into the repository

body:
## Problem

`third_party/go-nfs/helpers/memfs` (664 lines) is part of the vendored copy but nothing imports it: not this module, not the rest of go-nfs.

## Evidence

`grep -rn helpers/memfs third_party/go-nfs --include=*.go` finds no import; `wc -l third_party/go-nfs/helpers/memfs/*.go` = 664. The main module imports only `github.com/willscott/go-nfs`, `.../file` and `.../helpers`.

## Impact

664 lines of copied code that every go-nfs update must carry and every reviewer of `third_party/` must skim, for no use.

## Fix

Delete `third_party/go-nfs/helpers/memfs/`, and extend the copy instruction in `third_party/go-nfs/UPSTREAM.md` to "no tests, examples, CI files or helpers/memfs".

## Resolution
Removed third_party/go-nfs/helpers/memfs; UPSTREAM.md's update procedure excludes it.
title: Vendored go-nfs keeps the never-imported helpers/memfs package

body:
## Problem

The file exists so the module compiles on operating systems other than macOS and Linux, where every function returns "not supported". The README declares macOS and Linux as the only platforms, and nothing builds for others.

## Evidence

`internal/platform/platform_other.go:1`: `//go:build !darwin && !linux`; lines 15-27 are stubs returning `errUnsupported`, `nil` or their input.

## Impact

27 lines of flexibility nothing needs, kept in step with every signature change in the real implementations.

## Fix

Delete `internal/platform/platform_other.go`. A build for an unsupported OS then fails at compile time with `undefined: platform.Mount`, which is accurate.

## Resolution
Deleted internal/platform/platform_other.go; builds for other OSes now fail at compile time.
title: platform_other.go only turns a compile error into a runtime error

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. README.md:92-93 says: "rclone's own environment variables apply to the server too: `RCLONE_VFS_*`, `RCLONE_WEBDAV_*` and rclone's global ones such as `RCLONE_BWLIMIT`."

## Evidence

`RCLONE_BWLIMIT` is parsed into the global config (fs.RegisterGlobalOptions loads env at init), but the limit is only enforced by rclone's token bucket, which starts in `accounting.Start` (rclone fs/accounting/accounting.go:34-36 → token_bucket.go:110 `StartTokenBucket` sets `tb.curr`). `LimitBandwidth` (token_bucket.go:175-184) does nothing while `tb.curr[i]` is nil. `accounting.Start` is called only by rclone's cmd/cmd.go:424, fstest and librclone; davdrive never calls it (no `accounting.` or `GlobalOptionsInit` reference in any non-test file of this repo).

## Impact

A user who sets `RCLONE_BWLIMIT` to keep uploads from saturating their connection, as the README tells them they can, gets unthrottled transfers with no warning.

## Fix

Drop `RCLONE_BWLIMIT` from the example and say that rclone options needing rclone's command startup, such as bandwidth limits, do not apply. (Alternative, a code change: call `accounting.Start(ctx)` in server.start so the limit takes effect, then keep the sentence.)

## Resolution
README now says RCLONE_BWLIMIT does nothing: rclone starts its limiter in its own command, which davdrive does not run.
title: README promises RCLONE_BWLIMIT works, but davdrive never starts rclone's bandwidth limiter

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. README.md:92 lists the VFS environment variables as `RCLONE_VFS_*`, and README.md:95 says: "A leftover `RCLONE_VFS_READ_ONLY=true`, for example, gives a read-only mount."

## Evidence

rclone loads global option blocks from the environment with prefix "" (fs/registry.go `load` → `ConfigMap("", oi.Options, "", nil)`), and `optionEnvVars.Get` (fs/configmap.go:42-43) names each variable `OptionToEnv(key)` = `RCLONE_` + the option name upper-cased. The VFS option names (vfs/vfscommon/options.go) include `read_only`, `dir_cache_time` and `umask`, so the variables are `RCLONE_READ_ONLY`, `RCLONE_DIR_CACHE_TIME` and `RCLONE_UMASK`; only options whose names start with `vfs_` map to `RCLONE_VFS_*`. Checked with a program printing `vfscommon.Opt` against rclone v1.76.0: `RCLONE_VFS_READ_ONLY=true` leaves ReadOnly=false, `RCLONE_READ_ONLY=true` sets ReadOnly=true.

## Impact

A user chasing an unexpectedly read-only mount looks for `RCLONE_VFS_READ_ONLY`, does not find it, and misses the real cause, `RCLONE_READ_ONLY`; one setting `RCLONE_VFS_READ_ONLY` or `RCLONE_VFS_DIR_CACHE_TIME` on purpose gets no effect.

## Fix

State the rule rclone uses: each VFS option is `RCLONE_` plus its name upper-cased (`RCLONE_VFS_WRITE_BACK`, `RCLONE_DIR_CACHE_TIME`, `RCLONE_READ_ONLY`), and change the example to "A leftover `RCLONE_READ_ONLY=true`, for example, gives a read-only mount."

## Resolution
README states the rule (RCLONE_ plus the option name in capitals) with RCLONE_VFS_WRITE_BACK, RCLONE_DIR_CACHE_TIME, RCLONE_READ_ONLY; example now RCLONE_READ_ONLY=true.
title: README names VFS environment variables RCLONE_VFS_*, but rclone reads RCLONE_READ_ONLY, RCLONE_DIR_CACHE_TIME, RCLONE_UMASK

body:
## Problem

Contradiction. internal/server/server.go:168-169: "newRemote builds the webdav backend from the mount alone, never from an rclone config file." README.md:92-94 says `RCLONE_WEBDAV_*` environment variables apply to the server.

## Evidence

newRemote calls `ri.NewFs(ctx, m.Name, "", fs.ConfigMap(ri.Prefix, ri.Options, "", conf))` (server.go:181). rclone's `ConfigMap` (fs/configmap.go:144-147) adds `optionEnvVars{prefix: "webdav"}` whenever options are given, so every `RCLONE_WEBDAV_<OPTION>` the daemon inherits fills any option the mount does not set; only `url`, `vendor`, `user` and `pass` come from the mount and win over the environment.

## Impact

A reader trusting the comment concludes the environment cannot change the backend, and misses `RCLONE_WEBDAV_*` when a mount behaves unlike its config; the code comment and README disagree on the same fact.

## Fix

server.go:168-169: "newRemote builds the webdav backend from the mount, never from an rclone config file; options the mount does not set can still come from `RCLONE_WEBDAV_*` variables."

## Resolution
newRemote doc: built from the mount, never a config file; unset options can come from RCLONE_WEBDAV_*.
title: newRemote's doc says the webdav backend comes from the mount alone, contradicting README and the RCLONE_WEBDAV_* variables it reads

body:
## Problem

Missing. The Files table (README.md:150-155) lists `$XDG_STATE_HOME/davdrive/<name>.sock`, `.lock`, `.log` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/davdrive/` with no default, unlike the config path at README.md:63, which names `~/.config/davdrive/config.toml` first.

## Evidence

internal/config/config.go:65-72: `StateDir` falls back to `~/.local/state/davdrive` and `CacheDir` to `~/.cache/davdrive` when the variables are unset or relative (`xdgDir`, config.go:94-104). macOS does not set either variable.

## Impact

On macOS, where XDG variables are normally unset, a user looking for the log or the cache to clear has to read the source or a command's output to find it.

## Fix

Write the paths with their defaults, as the config path is: `~/.local/state/davdrive/<name>.sock` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/davdrive/…`) and `~/.cache/davdrive/` (or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/davdrive/`).

## Resolution
README file table introduced with the defaults: ~/.local/state and ~/.cache.
title: README's file table gives only $XDG_STATE_HOME and $XDG_CACHE_HOME, not the defaults used when they are unset

body:
## Problem

Contradiction. CONTRIBUTING.md:6-7 says mise "installs the pinned tools in `mise.toml`: golangci-lint v2 (configured by `.golangci.yml`), govulncheck, goreleaser and svu." CONTRIBUTING.md:30 says `mise install` installs "golangci-lint, govulncheck, goreleaser, svu, gobco".

## Evidence

mise.toml:16-21 pins five tools, including `"go:github.com/rillig/gobco" = "1.3.4"`, used by the `test-cov` task (mise.toml:45-59).

## Impact

The requirements list is the first place a contributor checks what mise will install; it disagrees with the tool list a few lines further down.

## Fix

CONTRIBUTING.md:7: "`.golangci.yml`), govulncheck, goreleaser, svu and gobco."

## Resolution
CONTRIBUTING requirements list gobco.
title: CONTRIBUTING's requirements list omits gobco, which mise.toml pins and the same file's mise install line names

body:
## Problem

Missing. The Layout table (CONTRIBUTING.md:15-22) maps every path of the repository, and its root-package row reads "`main.go`, `cmd_*.go` | The CLI: `mount`, `unmount`, `status` and the hidden `daemon` command"; `nfslog.go` appears in no row.

## Evidence

nfslog.go:10-18 defines `nfsLogger`, which routes go-nfs's messages into rclone's log at their own level; main.go `setupLogging` installs it with `nfs.SetLogger`. It is the only non-test root file outside `main.go` and `cmd_*.go`.

## Impact

A contributor looking for where go-nfs log levels are mapped (what `-v`/`-vv` show from the NFS server) finds no entry for it in the table meant to answer that.

## Fix

CONTRIBUTING.md:17: "| `main.go`, `cmd_*.go`, `nfslog.go` | The CLI: `mount`, `unmount`, `status` and the hidden `daemon` command; go-nfs logging |" (re-pad the column).

## Resolution
CONTRIBUTING layout table has an nfslog.go row.
title: CONTRIBUTING's layout table leaves out nfslog.go, the go-nfs log adapter in the root package

body:
## Problem

Stale. mise.toml:43-44: "internal/platform is measured through platform_unix.go alone, the only file its tests reach."

## Evidence

internal/platform/mount_darwin_test.go `TestMountToolErrors` calls `Mount` and `Unmount` (mount_darwin.go:12-27); internal/platform/platform_unix_test.go `TestIsMounted` calls `IsMounted` (mount_darwin.go:31-47 / mount_linux.go:61-74); internal/platform/mount_linux_test.go covers `privileged`, `Unmount` and `Mount`. The reason gobco measures only platform_unix.go is the GOOS clash the comment names first, not an absence of tests.

## Impact

A reader concludes that branch coverage loses nothing by skipping mount_*.go, when it leaves their tested branches unmeasured.

## Fix

mise.toml:43-44: "internal/platform is measured through platform_unix.go alone; the branches of mount_darwin.go and mount_linux.go go unmeasured."

## Resolution
mise.toml test-cov comment: mount_darwin.go and mount_linux.go branches go unmeasured.
title: mise.toml test-cov comment says platform_unix.go is the only internal/platform file the tests reach; they now reach mount_darwin.go and mount_linux.go too

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. main.go:134-135: "A busy mount is forced, since the server is going away either way."

## Evidence

main.go:150-155 retries forced after any unmount error, not only a busy mount (a failed `sudo -n`, for one). And the server does not go away either way: serveUntilStopped (main.go:186-195) keeps it running when unmountIfMounted reports the share still mounted and no failure occurred.

## Impact

A reader expects forcing only on EBUSY and believes the server always stops afterwards, the opposite of the keep-running rule serveUntilStopped's own comment explains.

## Fix

main.go:134-135: "A failed unmount is retried forced, since the server is about to stop."

## Resolution
unmountIfMounted doc: a failed unmount is retried forced, since the server is about to stop.
title: unmountIfMounted's doc says only a busy mount is forced and the server goes away either way

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The `mount` command's Long help (cmd_mount.go:42-43): "Mounting a share that is already mounted does nothing."

## Evidence

Without -f, `resume` prints "%s is already mounted at %s" and returns nil (cmd_mount.go:101-104). With -f, `mountForeground` returns "%s already has a server running (pid %d); stop it with: davdrive unmount %s" when a server answers, and the stale-mount error when only a mount exists (cmd_mount.go:270-280).

## Impact

The help a user reads for `mount -f` promises a harmless no-op and the command exits with an error instead.

## Fix

cmd_mount.go:42-43: "Mounting a share that is already mounted does nothing; with -f it is an error."

## Resolution
mount help: already mounted does nothing; with -f it is an error.
title: mount --help says mounting an already-mounted share does nothing; with -f it is an error

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. cmd_mount.go:149-150: "Until its own logging starts, the daemon's stderr (a panic, say) goes to the log file too."

## Evidence

`cmd.Stderr = logFile` (cmd_mount.go:174) holds for the daemon's lifetime. The daemon's logging (setupLogging, main.go) sets `MaxSize` to 10 MiB, so rclone's InitLogging takes the lumberjack branch (rclone fs/log/log.go:246-255), which never calls `redirectStderr`; only the no-rotation branch (log.go:227-235) does. stderr therefore stays the log file after logging starts.

## Impact

A reader concludes a panic after start-up is lost and goes looking elsewhere; it lands in the same log.

## Fix

cmd_mount.go:149-150: "The daemon's stderr (a panic, say) goes to the log file too, for its whole run: rclone's rotated log does not redirect stderr."

## Resolution
spawnDaemon comment: stderr goes to the log for the daemon's whole run.
title: spawnDaemon comment says the daemon's stderr goes to the log file only until its logging starts; it does for the whole run

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. cmd_mount.go:198-199: "logPath goes into the errors so the user knows where the daemon's own account of the failure is."

## Evidence

Only the timeout and empty-reply errors include it (cmd_mount.go:209, 211). An "error: <message>" reply returns `errors.New(strings.TrimPrefix(reply, "error: "))` (cmd_mount.go:214), with no log path.

## Impact

A maintainer relying on the comment assumes every start-up failure points at the log; the most common one, a refused password or bad URL, does not.

## Fix

cmd_mount.go:198-199: "The timeout and early-exit errors name logPath, so the user knows where the daemon's own account of the failure is."

## Resolution
parseReady doc: the timeout and early-exit errors name logPath.
title: parseReady's doc says logPath goes into the errors; the daemon's own error message is returned without it

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. cmd_unmount.go:45-46: "The control socket answers between uploads, so a run of failures means the server is stuck, not busy."

## Evidence

The control socket is an http.Server on its own goroutine (internal/server/control.go:85-97); its /status handler reads `s.vfs.Stats()` and answers while uploads run, which is how unmount prints "Waiting for N upload(s)" (cmd_unmount.go:131, 142).

## Impact

"Between uploads" suggests a busy server may legitimately go quiet, the opposite of the reasoning the constant relies on.

## Fix

cmd_unmount.go:45-46: "The control socket keeps answering while uploads run, so a run of failures means the server is stuck, not busy."

## Resolution
queryFailureLimit doc: the control socket keeps answering while uploads run.
title: queryFailureLimit's doc says the control socket answers between uploads; it answers during them

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. cmd_unmount.go:102-104: "waitForExit polls the control socket until the server is gone, reporting pending uploads meanwhile. Ctrl-C (ctx done) only stops the waiting".

## Evidence

cmd_unmount.go:123-126: after `queryFailureLimit` consecutive query errors it returns `notAnsweringAfterUnmount`, with the server possibly still running.

## Impact

The doc lists two exits and the function has three; a caller reading it does not expect a not-answering error.

## Fix

Add to cmd_unmount.go:104: "After queryFailureLimit failed queries in a row it gives up and reports the server as not answering."

## Resolution
waitForExit doc names the give-up after queryFailureLimit failed queries.
title: waitForExit's doc says it polls until the server is gone; it also gives up after queryFailureLimit failed queries

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. cmd_unmount.go:135-136: "reportPending prints the pending upload count when it changed since last".

## Evidence

cmd_unmount.go:139: `if pending == 0 || pending == last { return last }` — a change to 0 returns without printing.

## Impact

The doc misstates when output appears; a change to the zero case would be made against a wrong description.

## Fix

cmd_unmount.go:135-136: "reportPending prints the pending upload count when it changed to a non-zero value since last".

## Resolution
reportPending doc: prints when the count changed to a non-zero value.
title: reportPending's doc says it prints whenever the count changed; a drop to zero is never printed

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. internal/config/config.go:26: "EnvConfig overrides the config file path."

## Evidence

DefaultPath returns $DAVDRIVE_CONFIG when set (config.go:56-59), and main.go uses DefaultPath only as the default of the `--config` flag (`root.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&a.configPath, "config", config.DefaultPath(), …)`), so an explicit `--config` wins.

## Impact

The comment implies the variable beats everything; with both set, the flag wins.

## Fix

config.go:26: "EnvConfig replaces the default config file path; --config still overrides it."

## Resolution
EnvConfig doc: replaces the default path; --config still overrides it.
title: EnvConfig's doc says it overrides the config file path; --config overrides it

body:
## Problem

Stale. internal/config/config.go:64: "StateDir holds the control sockets and logs."

## Evidence

LockPath (config.go:224-225) is `filepath.Join(StateDir(), m.Name+".lock")`, the flock the daemon holds for its lifetime (internal/server/control.go:37-59).

## Impact

Someone cleaning up state from the comment's description misses the lock files, and README's file table (which lists them) disagrees with it.

## Fix

config.go:64: "StateDir holds the control sockets, lock files and logs."

## Resolution
StateDir doc lists lock files.
title: StateDir's doc lists sockets and logs; it also holds each share's lock file

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. internal/config/config.go:92-93: "Without a home directory the result is relative, which CheckDirs rejects."

## Evidence

xdgDir also builds DefaultPath (config.go:61). CheckDirs (config.go:79-89) loops over `StateDir(), CacheDir()` only, so with HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME unset but absolute XDG_STATE_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME, the relative config path `.config/davdrive/config.toml` passes and is resolved against the working directory.

## Impact

The comment claims a guard that does not exist for one of xdgDir's three callers.

## Fix

config.go:92-93: "Without a home directory the result is relative; CheckDirs rejects that for the state and cache directories."

## Resolution
xdgDir doc: CheckDirs rejects a relative result for the state and cache directories only.
title: xdgDir's doc says CheckDirs rejects a relative result; it checks only the state and cache directories, not the config path

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. internal/config/config.go:237-238: "password_command is the user's own shell command from their own config file, run as them, exactly like rclone's --password-command."

## Evidence

davdrive runs `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "/bin/sh", "-c", m.PasswordCommand)` (config.go:239). rclone runs `exec.Command(ci.PasswordCommand[0], ci.PasswordCommand[1:]...)` (rclone fs/config/crypt.go:198): a space-separated argv, no shell.

## Impact

A user porting an rclone `--password-command` relies on "exactly like" and gets shell parsing (quoting, `$`, pipes) where rclone had none.

## Fix

config.go:237-238: "password_command is the user's own shell command from their own config file, run as them through /bin/sh, as trusted as rclone's --password-command."

## Resolution
password_command comment: run through /bin/sh, as trusted as rclone's --password-command.
title: Password's comment says password_command runs exactly like rclone's --password-command; rclone runs argv, davdrive a shell

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. internal/fsys/fs.go:215-216: "A file in the way is os.ErrExist: NFSv4 CREATE relies on this to refuse a taken name."

## Evidence

fs.go:224-230 returns os.ErrExist only when an existing node is not a directory; an existing directory returns nil. third_party/go-nfs/nfs4_oncreate.go:55 calls MkdirAll with no existence check of its own, so CREATE of a name an existing directory holds answers NFS4_OK.

## Impact

The doc claims taken names are refused; half of them are not, which hides the CREATE defect routed below.

## Fix

fs.go:215-216: "A file in the way is os.ErrExist, which NFSv4 CREATE returns as NFS4ERR_EXIST; an existing directory is not an error."

## Resolution
MkdirAll doc: a file in the way is os.ErrExist (NFS4ERR_EXIST); an existing directory is not an error.
title: MkdirAll's doc says NFSv4 CREATE relies on it to refuse a taken name; a name taken by a directory is accepted

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. internal/server/control.go:17: "ErrNotRunning means no daemon answers on the control socket."

## Evidence

Query returns ErrNotRunning only for ENOENT or ECONNREFUSED (control.go:150-152): no socket file, or nothing accepting on it. A daemon that accepts but never replies yields the client timeout error instead, which main.go `state` keeps as `queryErr`, the "does not answer" case.

## Impact

"No daemon answers" describes exactly the hung case the code separates from ErrNotRunning; a caller treating them alike would stop guarding hung mounts.

## Fix

control.go:17: "ErrNotRunning means nothing listens on the control socket: no socket file, or a connection refused."

## Resolution
ErrNotRunning doc: nothing listens (no socket file, or connection refused).
title: ErrNotRunning's doc says no daemon answers; a hung daemon does not answer either and gets a different error

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. internal/server/auth.go:30-32: "so uid and 0 are admitted and every other uid and flavor is refused."

## Evidence

auth.go:41-43: `if proc == rpcProcNull { return true }` admits procedure 0 from any uid and any flavor, AUTH_NULL included; internal/server/auth_test.go "AUTH_NULL ping" asserts it, and the raw-RPC test sees another uid's NULL accepted (nfs_wire_test.go "ping from another user").

## Impact

A security-relevant doc overstates the check; a reviewer auditing access from the comment misses the exempted procedure.

## Fix

auth.go:31-32: "so uid and 0 are admitted and every other uid and flavor is refused, except for the NULL procedure, a ping that touches no state."

## Resolution
ownerOnly doc names the NULL-procedure exception.
title: ownerOnly's doc says every other uid and flavor is refused; NULL pings pass with any credential

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. third_party/go-nfs/server.go:40-41 (added by rpc-auth.patch): "Authorize, when set, is asked about every call before it is dispatched". third_party/go-nfs-UPSTREAM.md:57-58 repeats it: "sees the procedure number and the credential … of every call before dispatch".

## Evidence

third_party/go-nfs/conn.go:268-275: when `handlerFor` finds no handler for the program, version or procedure, the call is drained and answered with the RPC error before the Authorize check at conn.go:278.

## Impact

The upstream pull request text and the field doc promise a hook over all traffic; calls to unknown programs never reach it.

## Fix

Change both to "every call that has a handler": edit the comment in rpc-auth.patch and UPSTREAM.md:57-58, then rebuild third_party/go-nfs with the documented procedure.

## Resolution
rpc-auth.patch comment and UPSTREAM.md say every call that has a handler; vendored copy rebuilt from upstream 19d4715, upstream tests pass.
title: Authorize's doc (rpc-auth.patch and go-nfs-UPSTREAM.md) says it sees every call; calls with no handler are answered before it runs

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. third_party/go-nfs/server.go:180-181 (added by accept-retry.patch): "net/http's Serve retries the same errors."

## Evidence

net/http's Serve retries any `ne.Temporary()` (Go net/http/server.go:3583). `OpError.Temporary` treats accept ECONNRESET and ECONNABORTED as temporary (net/net.go:552-561), and `Errno.Temporary` is `EINTR || EMFILE || ENFILE || Timeout()` (syscall/syscall_unix.go:134-135). retryableAcceptError retries timeouts, EMFILE and ENFILE only.

## Impact

The comment, which is also the upstream change, claims parity with net/http that it does not have; a reviewer comparing the two finds the claim false.

## Fix

Patch comment: "net/http's Serve retries these too." Edit accept-retry.patch and rebuild third_party/go-nfs with the documented procedure.

## Resolution
accept-retry.patch comment: net/http's Serve retries these too; vendored copy rebuilt, upstream tests pass.
title: accept-retry.patch says net/http retries the same errors; net/http retries more of them

body:
## Problem

Test name misrepresents behaviour. internal/server/auth_test.go:40: `{"name padding is skipped", 1, authSys, authSysBody("hostname", owner, 20), true}`.

## Evidence

authSysBody pads the name to a multiple of 4 (auth_test.go:19-21); "hostname" is 8 bytes, so no padding byte is written. Padding is exercised by the "owner" case ("mac", one pad byte) and "unpadded name length" ("abcde", three).

## Impact

The case claims to cover padding and covers a name that needs none; a reader counts padding as tested twice when the named case adds nothing for it.

## Fix

Rename the case "name length a multiple of 4".

## Resolution
Case renamed "name length a multiple of 4".
title: TestOwnerOnly case "name padding is skipped" uses an 8-byte machine name, which has no padding

## Problem

Incorrect. helpers_test.go:384-385: "brokenReply answers every request with a server error, as a daemon that is shutting down or wedged can."

## Evidence

The daemon's control socket has one handler, `GET /status`, which always writes status 200 with JSON (internal/server/control.go:87-90); shutting down closes the listener (server.go Stop) and a wedged daemon times out. A 500 can only come from something other than a healthy davdrive daemon on the socket.

## Impact

The helper's stated reason is false; a reader believes the daemon has a 500 path worth handling.

## Fix

helpers_test.go:384-385: "brokenReply answers every request with a server error: a socket that answers, but not as a davdrive daemon does."

## Resolution
brokenReply doc: a socket that answers, but not as a davdrive daemon does.
title: brokenReply's doc says a shutting-down or wedged davdrive daemon can answer with a server error; it never does

## Problem

Incorrect. helpers_test.go:512-513: "isolateLogging restores rclone's and go-nfs's global logging setup when the test ends, since setupLogging changes it process-wide."

## Evidence

The cleanup restores `rlog.Opt`, the handler level and `nfs.Log` (helpers_test.go:521-525). setupLogging calls `rlog.InitLogging()`, which with a log file calls `Handler.setWriter(w)` and `Handler.setFormat` (rclone fs/log/log.go:257, 269); neither is restored, so later tests keep logging to the earlier test's file unless captureLogs's ResetOutput runs.

## Impact

A test author relying on the doc expects a clean logging state after isolateLogging and gets the previous test's log file as output.

## Fix

helpers_test.go:512-513: "isolateLogging restores rclone's options and level and go-nfs's logger when the test ends; the handler's writer and format stay as setupLogging left them (captureLogs resets the writer)."

## Resolution
isolateLogging doc lists what it restores and that the writer and format are not.
title: isolateLogging's doc says it restores the global logging setup; it leaves the log writer setupLogging installs

## Problem

Test description misrepresents behaviour. cmd_mount_test.go:469-470: "TestSpawnDaemonResourceFailures checks spawnDaemon reports what kept it from starting the daemon, and leaves none running."

## Evidence

The test body (cmd_mount_test.go:498-506) calls `reapDaemon` (a cleanup that kills any daemon still answering) and `checkErr`; it never calls `notRunning`, unlike TestMountBackgroundRefusals (cmd_mount_test.go:191-193).

## Impact

A spawnDaemon change that leaves a daemon behind passes this test silently, because the cleanup kills it without failing.

## Fix

Add `if !notRunning(t.Context(), m) { t.Error("a daemon is running after spawnDaemon failed") }` after `checkErr`, or drop "and leaves none running" from the comment.

## Resolution
TestSpawnDaemonResourceFailures now asserts nothing answers on the share's socket (path taken before setup moves the state dir).
title: TestSpawnDaemonResourceFailures says it checks no daemon is left running; nothing asserts it

## Problem

Incorrect. internal/server/nfs_wire_test.go:86-87: "On Linux the reserved-port rule refuses this unprivileged test program outright."

## Evidence

dialNFS uses `net.Dial` (nfs_wire_test.go:73-82), which takes an ephemeral source port whoever runs it; reservedPortListener refuses by source port (auth.go:89). The test passed in an Ubuntu 24.04 container running as root, refused the same way.

## Impact

The comment ties the refusal to privilege; a reader expects the test to behave differently as root, and it does not.

## Fix

nfs_wire_test.go:86-87: "On Linux the reserved-port rule refuses this test's connection outright: it comes from an unreserved port."

## Resolution
TestNFSServesOwnerOnly doc: refused for its unreserved source port.
title: TestNFSServesOwnerOnly says Linux refuses it as an unprivileged program; it is refused for its unreserved source port, as root too

## Problem

Test description misrepresents behaviour. internal/platform/mount_darwin_test.go:12-14: "TestMountToolErrors checks the command lines Mount and Unmount run, the user's mount_options included, and that the tool's message reaches the error."

## Evidence

Only the mount case's expected prefix includes the tool's text ("…: mount_nfs: "). The unmount and forced-unmount prefixes end at the command line plus ": " (mount_darwin_test.go:27-31), so `umount`'s "not currently mounted" and diskutil's "Unmount failed" are never asserted.

## Impact

A regression that drops the tool's message from Unmount errors passes while the comment says it is checked.

## Fix

Assert the messages: want `"/sbin/umount " + missingMountpoint + ": umount: "` and `"/usr/sbin/diskutil unmount force " + missingMountpoint + ": Unmount failed"`; or say the message is checked for mount only.

## Resolution
TestMountToolErrors asserts umount's and diskutil's messages too.
title: TestMountToolErrors says it checks the tool's message reaches the error; only the mount case does
